partners.mechanism_chain: SLC40A1 (HGNC:10608) —DISRUPTS→ Iron efflux from cells (GO:0006884); Iron efflux from cells (GO:0006884) —LEADS_TO→ Iron overload in tissues (HP:0003116); FTH1 (HGNC:3639) —DISRUPTS→ Cellular iron storage (GO:0006874); Cellular iron storage (GO:0006874) —LEADS_TO→ Free intracellular iron (CHEBI:29030); Free intracellular iron (CHEBI:29030) —INCREASES→ Neurodegeneration (HP:0002090); Free intracellular iron (CHEBI:29030) —INCREASES→ Brain iron accumulation (HP:0012388); Iron overload in tissues (HP:0003116) —INCREASES→ Free intracellular iron (CHEBI:29030). Loss-of-function mutations in SLC40A1 impair cellular iron efflux, leading to systemic iron overload (Hemochromatosis type 4). Concurrently, mutations in FTH1 impair cellular iron storage, resulting in increased free intracellular iron. This elevated free iron can contribute to neurodegeneration and specific iron accumulation in the brain (NBIA 9). Thus, both diseases converge on the dysregulation of free intracellular iron levels, though through distinct primary defects in iron export versus storage.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in SLC40A1 or CP do not lead to increased cellular iron or oxidative stress markers in relevant cell models or patient tissues, or identification of a lack of shared phenotypic features in individuals with compound heterozygosity for mutations in both genes. _(variant: Any common variants (AF > 0.01) in SLC40A1 or CP associated with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of oxidative stress resulting from iron dysregulation in these distinct genetic disorders could inform therapeutic strategies targeting iron chelation or antioxidant therapies for both hemochromatosis type 4 and aceruloplasminemia patients.
